title: GPX Track Point Counter: Count Every Point
description: Count trackpoints, route points and waypoints in a GPX file with the GPX Track Point Counter — the file's census, read locally. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a weekend file holding two tracks of 1,200 and 850 trackpoints, one 64-point route and 12 waypoints reports 2,126 points in total — counted by kind, not just in sum.
quick_answer: The GPX Track Point Counter inspects a GPX file and counts its points by kind — trackpoints (<trkpt>), route points (<rtept>) and waypoints (<wpt>). Load the file locally and read the census: the quickest structural X-ray a GPX file can get, before any deeper analysis begins.

body.t: 2 tracks (1,200 + 850 trkpt) + 1 route (64 rtept) + 12 wpt = 2,126 points. Reported by kind, the numbers already describe the file: a weekend's recording with one planned route riding along.

A 100-point file can span 500 km (a flight) while a 10,000-point file covers a 5 km run recorded every second. Count measures resolution, not size — the bounding box and route stats supply the geography.

popular_table.note: Counting is structural: the tool counts elements as the XML holds them, including points inside extensions-free plain files and multi-segment tracks alike.

faq: Extensions live inside trackpoints (heart rate, power) — they add data to a point, not points. The census counts the points; the channels are the analyzers' subject.
Does it count metadata or bounds corners?
No — only the three point elements. A file's <bounds> corners are summary values, not recorded points.
A <trkseg> with no points counts as zero and drags nothing — the census reports points, and an empty segment is structure without substance.
How fast is counting for huge files?
Counting is the cheapest operation a file can undergo — even million-point files tally quickly in the browser, long before rendering them would be wise.
Divide the count by the route's length from the stats tools — the density figure that predicts how smooth the track draws and how honest its elevation sum can be.
Can it count CSV or GeoJSON points instead?
Those formats have their own counters in the file family (rows and features) — this page speaks GPX elements specifically.
